main_text.l: Cùm habitaverint fratres pariter, & mortuus fuerit unus ex eis, & filius non fuerit ei, non nubito uxor mortui extrà viro extraneo. Cognatus ejus (hoc est, vel levir viduæ, vel patruelis, vel alius defuncti consanguineus) ingreditor ad eam, & capito eam sibi uxorem, affinitatem mý contrahito cum ea. Esto autem primogenitus, quem pepererit, statò nomine fratris sui defuncti, ne deleatur nomen ejus ex Israële. Quòd si noluerit vir ille accipere cognatam suam, tunc ascendito cognata ejus ad seniores, & dicito: Renuit cognatus meus sus-citare fratri suo nomen in Israële, non vult affinitatem contrahere mecum. Tunc accersunto illum seniores urbis, & loquuntur cum eo, & stato, ac dicito: Nolui accipere eam. Accedito postea cognata ejus ad ipsum in oculis seniorum, & solvito calceamentum ejus à pede ipsius, & spuito in faciem ejus, loquitorq;, ac dicito: Sic fiet viro, qui non ædificaverit domum fratris sui. Et vocator nomen ejus in Israële, domus discalceati, (hoc est, si conjugium hoc à seniori-bus persuaderi ipsi non poterit, publicâ ignomi-niâ coram judicio notabitur, propter exutum fraternum affectum erga defunctum, translatio-nemque juris ac potestatis publico hoc signo testabitur vidua. page.notes: Marginal number "28." in right margin is transcribed as a note. Left strip (edge of neighbouring page with margin text) omitted. The running head "septimi præcepti." and chapter title "CAPUT XVII." share the header line; both are kept as the running head. "mý" after affinitatem is an abbreviation mark read with some doubt: [?] not added as the mark is clear enough in context but could be a macron on y. The text ends mid-word "so-" at the line end; the rest continues on the next page. The Latin quotation from Deuteronomy is set in italic up to "discalceati,"; the explanatory parenthesis after it is roman.
